cover.title: 5 niche habits of founders who spot a drop before their users do

inner.title: watch the last 30 minutes
inner.body: ga4's real-time report only shows users from the last 30 minutes. after every deploy, open it and fire the page you just changed, because that window is the only place a break shows up before tomorrow.

inner.title: switch on suggested insights
inner.body: ga4 offers ready-made anomaly alerts for daily event count, views and conversions, with email notifications. most founders never turn the slider on, so the first person to see the drop is a customer.

inner.title: alert on a floor
inner.body: ga4 alerts can fire when a metric is less than a number you set, on an hourly, daily or weekly check. an anomaly alert only reads data it receives, so a deleted tag sends zero data and zero alerts.

inner.title: log every deploy time
inner.body: trackingplan's examples tie drops like a 40% add_to_cart decline to the release that stripped the tag from checkout pages. if you can't say when you last shipped, you can't tell a bug from a bad day.

inner.title: never judge yesterday
inner.body: reports for the last two days may be incomplete, so a scary yesterday is often a draft. judge trends on the day before yesterday, and use real-time for anything that can't wait.
